newsitem.title: ITALY: IMI buys 3pct of San Paolo.
newsitem.headline: IMI buys 3pct of San Paolo.

text.p: Italian investment bank IMI said in a statement on Wednesday it had bought a three percent stake in Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, paying the equivalent of 10,300 lire per share for the holding.
IMI already held almost two percent of the group and confirmed in the statement it would buy a further 0.18 percent holding to bring its total stake to five percent.
IMI announced earlier this month that it planned to take a five percent stake in San Paolo to become a core shareholder in the group ahead of its privatisation, planned for later in 1997.

It said it had bought the three percent holding from the San Paolo group. The money and shares will be transferred once bourse watchdog Consob has given its approval for San Paolo's privatisation prospectus.
San Paolo shares closed on Wednesday at 11,537 lire.

Spain's Banco Santander, Fiat holding IFI, Italian bank Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, and Italian insurer Reale Mutua Assicurazioni have also said they will become core shareholders in San Paolo bank. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
